### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. colorectal cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.458)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-4420097, Reactome:R-HSA-9664422)

**Proposed mechanism:** APC variant leading to loss of function —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:424); APC (HGNC:424) —DECREASES→ Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP1767); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP1767) —LEADS_TO→ Vascular malformation (HP:0001061); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP1767) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575). Loss-of-function variants in APC disrupt its function in regulating the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. Aberrant activation of this pathway contributes to the development of both vascular malformations (Disease A) and colorectal cancer (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** Absence of APC mutations in individuals with primary intraosseous venous malformation, or identification of a distinct, non-Wnt-related pathway as the primary driver of the vascular malformation. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic APC variants from gnomAD populations at a frequency that would preclude their role as a rare causal variant for disease A.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway could offer a shared therapeutic strategy for both conditions, although the specific manifestations and stages of disease would require tailored approaches.

#### 2. ACTB-associated syndromic thrombocytopenia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-4420097, Reactome:R-HSA-9664422, Reactome:R-HSA-2029482)

**Proposed mechanism:** ELMO2 (HGNC:17448) —DISRUPTS→ Rac1 signaling (GO:0035547); Rac1 signaling (GO:0035547) —DECREASES→ Cell adhesion molecules (GO:0019058); Cell adhesion molecules (GO:0019058) —LEADS_TO→ Primary intraosseous venous malformation (MONDO:0011744); ACTB (HGNC:87) —DISRUPTS→ Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010) —DECREASES→ Cell adhesion molecules (GO:0019058); Cell adhesion molecules (GO:0019058) —LEADS_TO→ Syndromic thrombocytopenia (MONDO:0100433). Loss-of-function mutations in ELMO2 disrupt Rac1 signaling, leading to decreased cell adhesion molecule function and primary intraosseous venous malformation. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in ACTB disrupt actin cytoskeleton organization, which also results in decreased cell adhesion molecule function and syndromic thrombocytopenia. The convergence is on the common pathway of regulating cell adhesion molecules.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of mutations in ACTB that lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in ACTB-associated syndromic thrombocytopenia, or mutations in ELMO2 that lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in primary intraosseous venous malformation, would falsify the proposed loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in ELMO2 or ACTB with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD would suggest incomplete penetrance or alternative etiologies.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ACTB and potentially converging pathways like cell adhesion molecule regulation in these distinct conditions could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both vascular malformations and bleeding disorders.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-4420097, Reactome:R-HSA-9664422, Reactome:R-HSA-2029482)
